To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the inefficiency of a cost-sharing protocol can be quantified, (ii) the inefficiency depends on the number of participants, and (iii) a simple protocol is approximately efficient for large enough numbers of participants.
the three properties are not mutually incompatible, that the inefficiency of a mechanism can be quantified, and that there is a mechanism that achieves all three properties.

(1) the inefficiency of a cost-sharing game can be measured by a single real number, (2) this number can be computed in polynomial time for a large class of games, and (3) this number can serve as a basis for a new mechanism design problem, which we call the problem of minimizing inefficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to quantify the inefficiency that arises from the tradeoff between the three goals.
the following question: What are the best cost-sharing mechanisms that simultaneously optimize all three goals?
the following questions: How much of the inefficiency of a cost-sharing problem can be attributed to the impossibility of achieving the three goals at once?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of cost-sharing mechanisms is an open problem.
there are no good cost-sharing mechanism design algorithms.
there is a fundamental trade-off between efficiency and incentive-compatibility in cost-sharing problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to study cost-sharing mechanisms with respect to all three of these goals simultaneously.
we show that, for a large family of cost-sharing problems, the three goals are mutually compatible after all, and that the cost of achieving them is small.
we have quantified inefficiency in cost sharing mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by relaxing the requirement of incentive-compatibility to only a small degree, one can achieve all three goals simultaneously.
it is possible to design a cost-sharing mechanism that is simultaneously incentive-compatible, budget-balanced, and efficient.
, by sacrificing a little bit of economic efficiency, we are able to achieve all three desirable properties.
